Radar cross section measurements were conducted at 35 GHz and 70 GHz.
Tower diameters ranged from 2.5 to 8 wavelengths in free space.
Dielectric constants of materials ranged from 1.01 to 1.2.
Four polyfoam materials were tested: rofoam, Eccofoam PS, Eccofoam S, and Styrofoam PS.
Echo area decreases with decreasing tower diameter faster than theoretical prediction over the measured range.
Echo area varies approximately as the square of the illuminated tower length.
The radar cross section at interference peaks is proportional to (Kr - 1)^2, tower radius, and tower length, and inversely proportional to wavelength.
Nulls in the echo area correspond to zeros of the Bessel function, approximately at D/h = 0.61 + N*0.50, N=0,1,2,...
Experimental null location errors were less than 0.15 wavelengths, about 2% at 70 GHz.
Echo area measurements have an accuracy of ±4 dB at 35 GHz and ±2 dB at 70 GHz.
Tuning towers can reduce echo area by 10 to 15 dB below peak values.
Echo areas of -35 dB·m² at 35 GHz and -25 dB·m² at 70 GHz were achieved for about 1 inch diameter towers.
Supports for towers must be designed to minimize their contribution to radar cross section.
Scattering mechanisms are influenced by cell size, material homogeneity, water content, surface finish, and machining.
The study confirms that polyfoam towers behave similarly to idealized lossless dielectric columns in radar scattering.
Measurements were averaged over a full 360° rotation of the towers.
Theoretical predictions are based on uniform, homogeneous, lossless dielectric column models.
The echo area pattern shows marked resonances with diameter.
The radar cross section is inversely proportional to the wavelength.
